input.brief: Benzo: sealed-bid auctions on Zcash testnet; bids stay time-locked until a public drand round, settle by 2-of-3 threshold signers, every result verifies offline; home is a draggable sky of doodles, one per real auction

direction.name: The product performs
direction.idea: Software is most convincing when it is doing its job in front of you. Instead of describing features, put small, true, working fragments of the product on the page: the actual control, with real content, responding to the pointer. A colour picker's loupe reads the page's own background and prints its value. A list tool lets you tick an item right there. A type-scale plugin sets the page's own headings. Find the one interaction that is the product and make the hero that interaction; then show each further capability as another fragment at real size. No dashboard collage, no browser frame, no screenshots shrunk until unreadable.
direction.composition: Hero: a short plain headline (4–6vw, left-aligned, upper-left third) and one sentence; the rest of the first screen is the main fragment at actual interface size, sitting directly on the page or on one flat stage colour, large enough to read every label. The fragment is built in HTML and works. Below, capabilities are a single-column sequence, each a row of two parts on a 5/7 split: a two-line statement on one side and the relevant fragment on the other, with the fragments varying in size and shape so the column never becomes a zigzag of equal blocks. Fragments are cropped pieces of interface (a menu, a row, a control, a panel edge), not whole windows. One section pins a fragment while three short statements change it.
direction.typography: The marketing type matches the product's interface type so the fragments and the page feel like one thing. Headline modest; interface text at its true size (13–15px) inside fragments.
direction.colour: Neutral ground. The product's own interface colours provide the colour. At most one flat stage colour behind fragments.
direction.imagery: The interface fragments are the main imagery: build them carefully with real labels, real numbers and sensible states (one hovered, one selected). Around them, two or three real pictures of the customer's world (found with scripts/assets.mjs), never stock of people at laptops.
direction.richness: Fidelity. A fragment with believable content and a real hover state is more interesting than any illustration. Spend the effort there.
direction.pitfalls: A fake interface made of grey bars and circles is the worst outcome; if you cannot build a believable fragment, change direction. Mark each fragment's root element with the attribute data-ui: inside it the product's own conventions apply (1px control borders, small radii, a shadow on its open menu) and the inspector leaves them alone; outside it the house rules hold as usual. data-ui is for cropped fragments only, never for a page wrapper. Do not put the fragment in a browser or laptop frame.

hero.name: Fragment on a shaped stage
hero.blueprint: A neutral ground. The headline occupies the upper-left third: two lines at clamp(52px, 5.2vw, 80px), medium weight, flush left on columns 1–6 at a 40px margin, starting 150px down. One supporting sentence at 18px, max 40ch, follows, then the single action as a small rectangular button. The rest of the screen belongs to one flat stage in a saturated colour: it spans columns 5–12, begins 42% down, and bleeds off the right and bottom edges. Its top-left corner is cut with the product's own shape using `clip-path` (a notch, a chamfer or a tab two columns wide), the only decoration on the page. On the stage, 56px in from its left and top edges, sits the main fragment of the interface at true size with labels at 13–15px, built in HTML and working: one panel or control about 620px wide, cropped by the bottom edge, never a whole window and never inside a browser or laptop frame. Mark its root with data-ui. Navigation is a plain row at 28px from the top: wordmark left and four text links right at 15px. Nothing overlaps the headline.
hero.mobile: The headline sits under the wordmark at 10vw on two lines, followed by the sentence at 16px and the button. The stage comes next at full width, bleeding off both sides and the bottom, its corner cut kept at 72px wide. The fragment sits 16px inside it at true size; if it is wider than the screen the right edge crops it rather than scaling it down.
hero.headline: A plain statement of what the product does in three to six words, two lines of up to about 16 characters each at 5.2vw.

type.note: An American gothic for headings over a sober transitional serif for reading, the pairing of a newspaper front page. Suits essays, annual reports, archives and finance pages that have real paragraphs.

palette.name: Sand and moss
palette.note: Sand grey holds the page with charcoal type, and one deep leaf-green band may close it. Moss green is reserved for buttons; brighter greens and blues arrive only through photographs.

motion.name: Shutter image
motion.description: The one hero or showcase image opens from an edge with a clip-path over about 1.1 seconds while the picture inside settles from 1.12 scale to rest. Use it once, on the image that matters most; later images simply are there. Recipe: 'Image shutter' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: One row, three states
sections.blueprint: The product's central row (a task, a transaction, a message, a deploy) is shown three times, one directly beneath the other, in three states: as it arrives, with the pointer on it and its actions revealed, and finished. Each copy is built at true size, 640px wide, with real names, amounts and times, its root marked data-ui; inside it the product's own control borders and radii apply. The copies sit in columns 4–9 with 56px between them and nothing framing them. In columns 1–3, right-aligned and level with each copy, one word at 22px in the soft ink names its state. Columns 10–12 stay empty. The middle copy is live: its checkbox or button works and turns it into the third state. The heading, two to four words at 28–32px, sits on column 4's left edge, 96px above the first copy, with no supporting line.
sections.mobile: Copies stack at full width with 16px margins and stay at true size; a row wider than the screen is cropped at its right end, never shrunk. Each state word sits beneath its copy at 17px in the soft ink, 10px away. 48px separates the three groups. Heading at 26px.

sections.name: Drag through the stages
sections.blueprint: A 50/50 split, 88svh tall: two flat fields meeting on a clean vertical edge, and one slider that drives both. Left field: the current stage as a clause of three to six words at clamp(40px, 4.6vw, 76px) on two lines, top-left from column 1, starting with its order word; it serves as the heading. Right field: one fragment of the product at true size, about 440px wide, centred, root marked data-ui, in the state that matches the clause. Along the bottom, crossing both fields inside 28px margins, a real range `<input>` with four stops: a solid track 8px tall, the part already passed in full ink, and a square thumb 32px across in the accent. Under the track, four stage names at 16px, the current one in full ink. Dragging, or the arrow keys, swaps the clause and the fragment's state with a 200ms crossfade; nothing depends on scroll.
sections.mobile: The fragment's field comes first, 46svh, the fragment at true size and cropped to its active region. The slider follows directly beneath on the seam, thumb 40px. Then the clause field: the clause at 9vw on two lines, with the four stage names under it in a two-by-two block at 15px.

sections.name: Two-ended rows, narrow column
sections.blueprint: A list in one narrow column, 520px wide, starting at 22% of the viewport width or centred. Every row is 34–38px tall with no box and nothing drawn between rows. Each row has two ends: at the left, a 16px round image (a face, a logo, a colour dot) followed after 8px by the name at 15–16px in full ink; at the far right of the column, a short value at 13px in the soft ink (a date, a price, a domain, an opening time) with tabular figures. Entries that need a sentence run to two lines at the left, and the value aligns with the first line. Groups are separated by 40px of space and begin with one plain word in the soft ink at the same size. A heading of two to four words at 24–28px in medium weight sits 32px above the first row. Holds 10–40 rows.
sections.mobile: The column fills the width with 20px margins. Rows are 44px tall for touch; the left image stays 16px. Long values wrap beneath the name at 13px, left-aligned with it, and the row grows. Group spacing is 32px.

sections.name: One quiet logo row
sections.blueprint: Only for real logos supplied by the project; if none are supplied, set the names in the text face at 22px in the same row and never draw stand-ins. The row reads as a sentence: it opens at the left margin with two to four plain words at 18px (the phrase that introduces the names), vertically centred on the logos, and five to seven logos follow on the same line, spread to the right margin with `justify-content: space-between`. Every logo is normalised to one optical height (28–32px for wordmarks, 36px for compact marks) and one colour, the page ink, using single-colour SVGs with `fill: currentColor`. The band is tall and almost empty: 120–150px of ground above and below the row, no box, no background change and no separate heading. Logos stay still; nothing scrolls or fades at the edges.
sections.mobile: The opening words sit alone on the first line at 17px. Logos follow in a grid of two per row, each 26px tall and left-aligned in its cell, with 36px between rows. Show six at most; there is no sideways scrolling.

sections.name: First step, already open
sections.blueprint: The page ends with the product's first screen already open. A full-bleed field in the accent colour, 90svh tall. Right, in columns 7–11, vertically centred: the product's own create dialog at true size, 440px wide, root marked data-ui, with its real title ('Name your workspace'), one text field holding an editable, believable example, one two-option segmented choice and its primary button. Inside the fragment the product's conventions apply, including the shadow its dialog normally casts. The field accepts typing, the choice switches, and the primary button is the page's only action: it carries the typed value into sign-up. Left, in columns 1–5, anchored to the bottom with 40px margins: the closing line, two to four words at clamp(56px, 7vw, 112px), leading 0.92, on two lines, and under it one sentence at 17px saying what happens after the button. The upper-left stays empty.
sections.mobile: The closing line leads at 13vw on two lines, top-left, with its sentence beneath at 16px. The dialog follows at full width inside 16px margins, at true size, its primary button 52px tall and full width. The field is at least 84svh; the dialog sits in its lower half.

sections.name: A single quiet line
sections.blueprint: No footer block at all. After at least 30svh of empty page ground, one baseline 30px above the bottom edge carries three items in the page's ordinary small text size (14–16px), the same size and weight as the navigation: at the left margin, what this is in three or four words; centred, two to five links separated by 24px of space; at the right margin, the year and a privacy link. Use a three-column grid (1fr auto 1fr) so the centre group is truly centred whatever the side lengths. No logo, no background change, no line above it, no columns. Links are in the full ink; the rest in the softer ink. If the page has a narrow text column, the three items may instead sit on that column's left edge as one wrapped line. The restraint only works if the page above has already made its invitation.
sections.mobile: Three short lines at 14px on the left margin with 8px between them: the description, the links on one wrapped line, then year and privacy. Links stay in the full ink. Leave 20svh of empty ground above and 24px below.

references.name: Shelf
references.idea: Saves scattered across a dozen places are funnelled into one searchable shelf, shown literally by tumbling source chips and a panel edge that narrows to a point.
references.hero: An off-white panel sits inside a 12px warm-grey page frame. A compact floating nav about 880px wide: logo left, three links and a lime waitlist button right. Centred stack: a small grey pill badge with a sparkle icon, then a two-line headline in General Sans Semibold at about 5.8vw with tight tracking, one word of which sits on a lime rounded-rectangle highlight; a two-line grey subhead; an email field with its button nested inside one rounded outline, 460px wide. From 75% down, the top of a bordered app window rises, and a larger search bar holding a half-typed query overlaps it with a soft shadow.
references.type: General Sans Semibold for headings (84px hero, 40 to 50px section heads, -0.03em); Switzer for everything else at 14 to 20px, mostly mid-grey. About four sizes. The one flourish is a headline word set on a coloured block.
references.colour: #fbfbf9 #f2f1ed #1b1b19 #9ee86f #e9e9e6 — Warm off-whites and soft charcoal with one lime green: the nav button, the highlighted word, small tags and a full-colour closing block.
references.imagery: Vector mock-ups of the app: a bordered window with sidebar and save cards, an enlarged search field, tiny wireframe thumbnails in step cards. No photography. Angled pill chips with small source icons act as illustration.
references.layout: Centred column inside large rounded off-white panels separated by the grey page frame. Mostly stacked heading-plus-subtext blocks, one left and right split, one narrow accordion column. Panel edges are shaped: one ends in a shallow downward chevron.

sections.description: A centred heading and two-line subtext are partly covered by about nine grey pill chips, each naming a save source with a small icon, rotated at random angles as if dropped. The panel's bottom edge is a shallow V pointing down at centre; from its tip a thin vertical line descends about 80px to a second centred heading, subtext and an empty search field, so the layout itself draws a funnel.

A rounded white panel split in two. Left, from a 10% inset: a small lime tag with icon, a two-line heading at about 50px and two short grey paragraphs, vertically centred. Right, from 53% to 90%: three stacked rounded grey cards about 130px tall, each with a white thumbnail tile at left (a tiny wireframe or the logo) and at right a black numbered dot, a bold one-line title and a line or two of grey text.

A lime rounded block about two-thirds of the width, flanked by narrower lime blocks at left and right separated by 14px gaps, as if cropped from a row. Inside, left-aligned and vertically centred: a 40px heading, two lines of small text and a white email field with the button nested in it. A one-line footer sits on a white strip below.

steal: Shape a section's bottom edge into a chevron and run a hairline from its tip to the next heading, turning 'many into one' into layout.
Overlap an enlarged, half-typed search field onto the product window so the hero shows the key interaction rather than a whole screenshot.
Frame the page as rounded panels inside a slightly darker margin so sections read as stacked sheets.

references.name: Typewave
references.idea: A plugin about type scales sold on a near-black page where flat saturated fields (orange, lime, blue) act as stages for the plugin's own dark interface.
references.hero: Near-black field. Nav row at the top: pixel-block logo and wordmark left, four plain links centred (one carrying a tiny lime tag), a cream rectangular button with a Figma glyph right. The headline sits centred around mid-height: three lines at about 6.7vw, medium weight, off-white, with the third line recoloured pale lime. Below it a three-line 18px paragraph held to about 45% of the width, then a small cream button repeating the nav action. About 150px lower, the top edge of a flat orange slab, 70% of the viewport wide with barely rounded corners, peeks over the fold; it holds the plugin window.
references.type: Roobert throughout: weight 500 for the 96px headline with slight negative tracking, 16-18px body, 28px card headings, about four sizes in all. Sentence case everywhere; the only emphasis device is recolouring one headline line.
references.colour: #0f0f0e #191918 #e6e3da #f88616 #e4f283 #1463ff — Warm near-black ground with cream text. Orange, lime and electric blue never colour paragraphs; they only fill the rectangles behind product screenshots and the matching step-number chips.
references.imagery: Dark plugin windows with a soft drop shadow, floated centred on flat saturated rectangles (orange, lime, blue, one pink); the rectangles are near square-cornered and inset inside a slightly lighter dark card.
references.layout: Centred hero, then a 1000px container of full-width dark cards, each split one-third text and two-thirds colour stage. Export features alternate text and tile left to right. A small two-button bar stays pinned bottom-centre.

sections.description: Three stacked cards in a slightly lighter black, each about 1000 by 350px. Left third: a 16px square number chip in the card's accent colour at the top, a three-line 28px heading under it, and a grey 12px paragraph pushed to the card's bottom edge, leaving a tall gap between. Right two-thirds: a flat colour rectangle inset 16px with the dark plugin window centred and shadowed on it. Cards differ only by hue: lime, orange, blue.

Between demo blocks a single left-aligned sentence at about 36px sits alone on black with some 300px of space above and below. Its words light up from dark grey to cream one after another as you scroll, so mid-capture the sentence trails off into the background. The pinned two-button bar is the only other element on screen.

Export options as alternating rows. One side: a square colour tile (lime, then orange) holding a code-panel screenshot. Other side: a 24px heading, a five-line grey paragraph and a row of three or four small monochrome tool logos. Tile and text swap sides on each row, and the tiles are staggered vertically so one row's tile overlaps the next row's text band.

steal: Stage dark UI screenshots on flat saturated rectangles instead of on the page background, so the colour does the branding and the UI stays legible.
Pin the paragraph to the bottom of a tall card and the heading to the top so the gap between them becomes the card's composition.
Colour-key each step: the number chip and the stage behind the screenshot share one hue and nothing else on the card uses it.

references.name: Fynza
references.idea: Bookings are drawn as avatar dots whose orange flow lines merge into a single vertical spine, which then runs down the page as the axis for the partner list, the cash-flow timeline and the step cards.
references.hero: Warm grey ground with a fine white dot texture and a peach gradient bleeding down from the top edge. A floating white pill navbar 80% wide holds the logo left and a language switch plus outlined and orange pill buttons right. Centred stack: a white pill badge with overlapping partner-logo dots, a two-line extra-bold uppercase headline at 4.2vw in slate navy with two words in orange, two lines of grey 18px text, an orange pill button. Around the button five round avatar photos with small booking labels sit at staggered heights across the full width; thin orange curves, two dashed, flow down from each and converge at bottom centre.
references.type: Golos Text only: weight 800 uppercase at 60px for every section headline with slight negative tracking, 18px regular grey body, about 24px semibold for card titles, tiny uppercase captions. A wide extended logo wordmark. Roughly four sizes; hierarchy relies on weight and colour.
references.colour: #edecea #ffffff #f4bba8 #f2561d #3f4f6e #1a2e7a — Warm grey and white with peach gradients fading in at section tops and bottoms; orange carries buttons, flow lines and highlighted headline words; one deep royal-navy slab near the end.
references.imagery: Round avatar photos, partner logo discs, sunny travel photographs inside rounded cards with white UI snippets floating on top, and illustrated vintage postage stamps tilted and scattered around the final call to action.
references.layout: Centred container of about 1150px; every section opens with a small white pill label and a two-line uppercase headline. A single orange vertical line runs through the page centre linking hero, logo list, timeline and step cards. Sections alternate grey, peach fade and one navy slab.

sections.description: Directly under the hero the converged orange line becomes a vertical spine and partner brands hang off it in two columns: logo then name on the left, name then logo on the right. Rows are separated by dashed horizontal rules with small orange dots where they cross the spine. There is no heading, so it reads as a continuation of the hero diagram.

Problem timeline on the centre spine: small rounded-square chips labelled by week sit on the line. Events alternate left and right, each joined to its chip by a dashed horizontal line ending in a small coloured amount tag (red for outflow, green for income), with a bold label and two lines of grey text. A red-tinted rounded note sits on the spine as the conclusion while the background fades to saturated peach.

Three large white rounded cards stacked on the spine, each a two-column split that alternates sides: on one side an orange numbered disc, a three-line semibold title and a small grey paragraph; on the other a rounded travel photograph with a white UI card or a cluster of logo discs floating over it. The orange line passes behind the gaps between cards.

Dotted peach-to-white field with a centred two-line uppercase headline, one word in orange, and an orange pill button. Six illustrated vintage travel stamps and round stickers are scattered around it at slight rotations, three above and three below, some tucked under the navbar. A tiny two-line legal footer sits directly underneath, centred, with no separate footer band.

steal: Turn the hero illustration's lines into a page-long spine: let the curves converge at the fold and continue as the axis for the next section's list and timeline.
Show the customer's own unit of value (a booking with name, party size and price) as small avatar chips instead of a dashboard screenshot.
End on a themed sticker scatter (illustrated stamps at varied tilt) around the last call to action rather than a plain coloured band.
